reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be the full finite-dimensional real Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure and canonical ordinary volume, including dimension zero. All approved section instances belong to the contract. Let V:E->R, alpha,beta:NNReal and eta:R. Assume alpha cast to R is strictly positive, alpha<=beta, V is C2, and for every x,b:E both bounds hold:
  alpha*||b||^2 <= (fderiv R (fderiv R V) x b) b,
  (fderiv R (fderiv R V) x b) b <= beta*||b||^2.
Assume eta>0 and beta*eta<=1. Define the actual measures, potential and real continuous-linear-functional-valued function
  mu=volume.tilted(x->-V(x)),
  J=map((x,g)->(x,x+sqrt(eta)*g),mu.prod(stdGaussian E)),
  W_y(z)=V((y+z)/2)+||z-y||^2/(8*eta),
  s_y(z)=-(1/2) scalar-multiplied by fderiv R V ((y+z)/2) -(1/(4*eta)) scalar-multiplied by innerSL R (y-z).
Equivalently, for every direction a:E,
  s_y(z)[a]=-(1/2)*(fderiv R V ((y+z)/2) a)-<y-z,a>_E/(4*eta).
This is the unnormalized parameter-y directional score defined by the actual formula; it is neither the negative z-gradient nor a centered normalized score. All measure operations are actual: normalized Gibbs tilt, independent product with the standard finite real Hilbert Gaussian, and pushforward.
There exist kernels R,S:E->Measure E such that both are Markov kernels, R is a true conditional kernel disintegrating J.map Prod.swap, and for every y, S(y)=(R(y)).map(x->2*x-y).
For every y:E, S(y)=volume.tilted(z->-W_y(z)), W_y is C2, exp(-W_y) is volume-integrable and its volume integral strictly positive. There exists for this y one real-linear partial operator D:Lp R 2 (S(y)) ->partialLinear[R] Lp E 2 (S(y)) with dense domain in the actual scalar L2 space, D closable and D.closure closed. Its graph is exactly the smooth compact-function/gradient pairs: for every scalar a and vector H, (a,H) is in D.graph iff there exists a smooth compactly supported real phi with a=phi S(y)-almost everywhere and H=gradient(phi) S(y)-almost everywhere.
This SAME D simultaneously has all the following properties:
(1) For every c:R, there exists u in D.closure.domain such that its scalar quotient representative equals the constant function x->c S(y)-almost everywhere and D.closure(u)=0 in vector L2(S(y)).
(2) For every u in D.closure.domain, D.closure(u)=0 if and only if there exists c:R such that its scalar representative is c S(y)-almost everywhere.
(3) For every direction a:E, the real function z->s_y(z)[a] is C1. For every z:E its actual Riesz gradient satisfies
  ||gradient(q->s_y(q)[a])(z)||_E <= ((1/eta-alpha)/4)*||a||_E.
For this same directional function there exists hp:MemLp (z->s_y(z)[a]) 2 (S(y)), and there exists hq:MemLp (gradient(z->s_y(z)[a])) 2 (S(y)), such that the actual ordered pair of scalar/vector quotient classes (hp.toLp the directional-score function,hq.toLp its actual gradient) belongs to this SAME D.closure.graph.
One common R,S pair precedes every y; each y has one D preceding ALL constants c, ALL closure-domain u and ALL directions a. Constant-domain witnesses and score L2 proof witnesses are produced after their respective universal inputs. Each directional gradient bound is all-point, and its coefficient is exactly (1/eta-alpha cast)/4; the eta cap together with alpha<=beta makes it nonnegative without adding a separate assumption. No alternate D is selected for a constant, u or direction. All y have the stated density/operator conclusions, while conditional disintegration retains its usual version scope. No extra equality between two conditional kernels is asserted.
All original/operator/score L2 classes, graph links and constant AE identities use S(y); the partition integrability and integrals use ordinary volume. Actual standard measurable representatives are used, with AE identities only rather than exact pointwise/support identities. No rough classical Hessian, covariance/centered-score statement, spectral-gap or further functional inequality, centered-residual/epsilon-zero/range theorem, complete adjoint/core, main/cost composition theorem, or jointly measurable fiber/constant/direction selection is concluded.
